rules.action: New-generation thin-strut drug-eluting stent (DES) recommended for ALL PCI indications, irrespective of presentation, lesion type, planned DAPT duration, or anticoagulant therapy.
Bioresorbable scaffolds (BRS) are NOT recommended outside clinical studies due to higher scaffold thrombosis and TVF rates compared with contemporary DES.
Post-dilate with NC balloon sized to vessel reference to achieve full apposition. Confirm expansion with intravascular imaging in complex cases.

Deploy distal stent first, work proximally. Plan overlap zones (≥3mm, avoid side branches). Post-dilate each segment with NC balloon before deploying the next. Total stent length ≥28mm qualifies as complex PCI (mandatory imaging).
Ultra-thin strut DES preferred — facilitates SB rewiring and reduces jailing. Size to distal MV reference diameter (Murray's law).

Size MV stent 1:1 to distal MV reference for bifurcation cases; expand proximally with POT to proximal LM size. For shaft/ostial disease, size to proximal reference. Proximal edge must not protrude into the aorta. Confirm MSA with IVUS.

DES and BMS are comparably effective in SVG PCI (DIVA, ISAR-CABG). Use slightly undersized diameter with generous length to minimise plaque extrusion. Avoid high-pressure post-dilation unless imaging shows inadequate expansion.
Avoid post-dilatation; if required, size 1:1 — never oversize.
Target complete revascularisation where feasible; stage if haemodynamic reserve is limited. Minimise stent length per vessel to reduce ischaemic time.
Complete revascularisation recommended for haemodynamically stable patients with multivessel disease. May be performed during index procedure or staged within 45 days.
Accept a longer procedure to ensure an optimal stent result. Discuss bailout strategy for abrupt closure with the team before wiring. Imaging-guided optimisation is mandatory.
rules.caution: A failed stent in the only remaining coronary is catastrophic — there is no haemodynamic reserve for an inadequate result.
